metadata.course: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology
metadata.attribution: Original scope and sequence authored for the Luminfest Learning Harness, dedicated to the public domain under CC0.
metadata.scope: Structure only: concept titles, unit order and prerequisite intent. No third-party curriculum text is reproduced, and no restricted source is ingested.
metadata.description: A full-year introductory biology course: the process of science and the chemistry of life, cell structure and transport, photosynthesis and respiration, cell division and reproduction, molecular genetics and heredity, evolution and classification, homeostasis in body systems and plants, ecology, and human impact and sustainability.

id_namespace.reason: Concept ids are global; the prefix keeps this course disjoint from the shipped courses that share concept titles.

textbook_alignment.link_only_note: OpenStax Biology 2e reports CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and is carried as a link-only study reference: never stored, quoted or used as an anchor.

Foundations of Biology: Characteristics of Life & Levels of Organization

concepts.title: Active Transport Against a Gradient
concepts.summary: Active transport spends ATP to move solute against its gradient, as the sodium-potassium pump does by exporting three sodium ions for every two potassium ions it imports, and it stores the work as an electrochemical gradient.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Adaptive Immunity Is Specific and Remembers
concepts.summary: B and T lymphocytes whose receptor matches an antigen are selected and clonally expanded, and the memory cells left behind make a second response faster and stronger, which is the basis of vaccination.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Allopatric and Sympatric Speciation
concepts.summary: Allopatric speciation begins when a geographic barrier divides populations, while sympatric speciation arises within one area, often through polyploidy or a shift in mating preference.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Animal Body Plans and Vertebrate Groups
concepts.summary: Animals are multicellular heterotrophs with tissues and, in most phyla, bilateral symmetry, and vertebrates divide into fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals by their skeletal and reproductive features.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: ATP Hydrolysis as the Energy Currency
concepts.summary: Hydrolysing ATP to ADP and phosphate releases usable energy because separating the negatively charged phosphate groups is exergonic, and coupling that step to an endergonic reaction is how the cell pays for work.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Balancing Water, Solutes and Heat
concepts.summary: Osmoregulation holds solute concentration by adjusting water gain and loss, and thermoregulation balances heat from metabolism and the environment against heat lost by evaporation and radiation.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Biodiversity Supports Ecosystem Function
concepts.summary: A community with more species usually keeps functioning when conditions change, because different species respond differently, so diversity works as insurance rather than decoration.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Carbohydrates and Lipids as Fuel and Structure
concepts.summary: Sugars and starch store readily mobilised energy while cellulose and chitin give rigid structure, and lipids store about twice the energy per gram because their hydrocarbon chains are more reduced.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Carbon and Energy Balance Between the Pathways
concepts.summary: Photosynthesis fixes inorganic carbon into sugar using light energy and respiration oxidises that sugar back to carbon dioxide and water, so the two pathways cycle carbon while energy passes one way through the ecosystem.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Carbon and Nitrogen Cycle Between Pools
concepts.summary: Carbon moves between the atmosphere, living matter and sediments through photosynthesis, respiration and combustion, while atmospheric nitrogen must be fixed by bacteria before most producers can use it.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Checkpoints and Cyclin Control
concepts.summary: The G1, G2 and spindle checkpoints block progress until their conditions are met, and they are enforced by cyclin-CDK complexes whose levels rise and fall with the cycle.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Circulation Moves Materials Between Surfaces
concepts.summary: A circulatory system connects exchange surfaces to every cell, and a double circulation sends blood through the lungs at low pressure before the heart drives it around the body at high pressure.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Cladistics and Shared Derived Characters
concepts.summary: Cladistics groups organisms by shared derived characters, so a valid group contains an ancestor and all of its descendants, which is why reptiles that exclude birds do not form a clade.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Cohesion, Adhesion and Thermal Buffering
concepts.summary: Hydrogen bonds make water cohesive, so a continuous column can be pulled up a xylem vessel, and give water a specific heat of 4.18 joules per gram kelvin that buffers temperature change.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Competition, Predation and Symbiosis
concepts.summary: Two species competing for one limiting resource cannot coexist indefinitely unless they divide it, while predation, mutualism, commensalism and parasitism each change the two populations in a different direction.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Conservation Strategies
concepts.summary: A protected area works only if it is large, connected and enforced, and ex situ measures such as seed banks and captive breeding complement it for species that cannot persist in the wild.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Control Groups and Confounding Variables
concepts.summary: A control group holds every condition constant except the treatment, so a difference in outcome can be credited to the treatment rather than to a confounder such as temperature or age.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Correlation, Causation and Uncertainty
concepts.summary: A correlation shows that two variables change together but not that one causes the other, and overlapping error bars mean the difference between two means is not resolvable at that sample size.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Costs and Benefits of Asexual Reproduction
concepts.summary: Asexual reproduction copies the parent quickly and needs no mate, but it produces genetically uniform offspring, so one change in the environment can remove the whole clone.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Coupled Reactions and Phosphorylation
concepts.summary: A coupled reaction pairs an exergonic step with an endergonic one through a shared intermediate, and phosphorylation transfers a phosphate from ATP to a substrate so that the substrate can react.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: CRISPR and Gel Electrophoresis
concepts.summary: CRISPR-Cas9 cuts a chosen sequence guided by a matching RNA, and gel electrophoresis then separates the resulting fragments by size because shorter fragments travel farther through the gel.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Crossing Over in Prophase I
concepts.summary: Homologous chromosomes exchange segments at chiasmata during prophase I, so a chromatid can carry alleles from both grandparents and the resulting gametes are recombinants.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Cytokinesis in Plants and Animals
concepts.summary: An animal cell pinches off with a contractile ring of actin and myosin, whereas a plant cell builds a cell plate from vesicles because a rigid wall cannot be pinched.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Dehydration Synthesis and Hydrolysis
concepts.summary: Monomers join by dehydration synthesis, which removes a water molecule at each new bond, and polymers are split by hydrolysis, which adds water back at that bond.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Differentiation from One Genome
concepts.summary: Every cell of an organism carries the same genome, so differentiation into distinct types comes from expressing different gene sets rather than from losing genes.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Diffusion and Osmosis
concepts.summary: A substance diffuses down its concentration gradient without energy input, and water crosses a selectively permeable membrane by osmosis toward the side with the higher solute concentration, so a cell in a hypertonic solution shrinks.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Directional, Stabilising and Disruptive Selection
concepts.summary: Directional selection shifts a trait's mean, stabilising selection removes both extremes, and disruptive selection favours both extremes and can split one population into two phenotypic groups.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Ecological Niches and Resource Partitioning
concepts.summary: A species' niche is the full set of conditions and resources it uses, and two species whose niches overlap heavily must partition those resources or one will exclude the other.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Endomembrane System and Protein Traffic
concepts.summary: Proteins made on the rough ER are folded and modified as they pass through the endomembrane system, then sorted by the Golgi apparatus into vesicles addressed to the membrane, a lysosome or the exterior.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Epigenetic and Post-transcriptional Control
concepts.summary: Methylation of DNA and modification of histones can silence a gene heritably without changing its sequence, and a microRNA can block translation or degrade a transcript after it is made.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Exchange Surfaces and the Surface-Area Constraint
concepts.summary: An exchange surface works only when it is thin, moist and large relative to the body's volume, which is why lungs fold into alveoli and intestine into villi rather than relying on the skin.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Exponential Growth and Its Limits
concepts.summary: A population with unlimited resources grows at a rate proportional to its size and so rises exponentially, but resources, disease and predation eventually reduce that rate.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Fermentation Regenerates NAD+
concepts.summary: Without oxygen the electron transport chain stalls, so fermentation reduces pyruvate to lactate or to ethanol and carbon dioxide purely to regenerate NAD+ and keep glycolysis running.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Fitness and Differential Reproduction
concepts.summary: Fitness is the relative contribution of a genotype to the next generation, so a trait that raises survival while lowering reproduction can still be selected against.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Food Webs and Keystone Species
concepts.summary: A food web records the many feeding links in a community, and a keystone species holds that web together out of proportion to its abundance, so its removal reshapes the community.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Fossils and Transitional Forms
concepts.summary: The fossil record places organisms in a historical order, and a transitional fossil such as Tiktaalik combines features of two groups in the order that common ancestry predicts.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Genotype, Phenotype and Dominance
concepts.summary: Genotype is the allele combination and phenotype the observable trait, so a heterozygote whose phenotype matches the homozygous dominant still carries a hidden recessive allele.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Glycolysis and Pyruvate Oxidation
concepts.summary: Glycolysis splits glucose into two pyruvate molecules in the cytoplasm with a net gain of two ATP and two NADH, and each pyruvate is then decarboxylated to acetyl-CoA for the citric acid cycle.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Habitat Loss and Fragmentation
concepts.summary: Converting land to farmland, roads and cities removes habitat and cuts what remains into isolated patches, and small patches lose species faster because their populations are smaller and cannot exchange migrants.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Homology, Analogy and Vestigial Structures
concepts.summary: Homologous structures share an underlying anatomy inherited from a common ancestor even when their functions differ, whereas analogous structures do the same job from different origins, so only homology indicates relatedness.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Hormones as Slower, Broadcast Signals
concepts.summary: A hormone travels in blood to cells that carry its receptor, so a steroid hormone enters the cell and alters transcription while a peptide hormone binds a surface receptor and triggers a second messenger.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Hypotheses as Testable Explanations
concepts.summary: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation stated so that a prediction follows from it, which is why "the plant wilted because the soil dried out" can be tested and "the plant wilted for no reason" cannot.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Incomplete Dominance and Codominance
concepts.summary: In incomplete dominance the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype, as pink snapdragons do, while in codominance both alleles are expressed separately, as in AB blood type.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Independent and Dependent Variables
concepts.summary: The independent variable is the condition the experimenter sets and the dependent variable is the one measured, so a valid test changes only the independent variable between groups.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Independent Assortment of Homologues
concepts.summary: Each homologous pair orients independently at metaphase I, so a human gamete is one of about eight million combinations before crossing over adds more.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Innate Immunity Is Fast and Non-specific
concepts.summary: The innate response uses barriers, phagocytes and inflammation to answer any invader within hours and without memory, so it slows an infection but does not target one pathogen in particular.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Levels of Organization from Molecule to Biosphere
concepts.topic: Characteristics of Life & Levels of Organization
concepts.summary: Biological organisation runs from organelle to cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism, population, community, ecosystem and biosphere, and each level shows properties its parts do not.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Life Histories and Age Structure
concepts.summary: An r-selected species produces many offspring with little care while a K-selected species produces few with heavy care, and a population's age structure predicts whether it will grow or shrink next.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Light and Electron Microscopy
concepts.summary: A light microscope resolves about 200 nanometres and can view living cells, while an electron microscope resolves below one nanometre by using electron wavelengths but needs fixed, dehydrated specimens.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Light Reactions in the Thylakoid
concepts.summary: Photosystem II splits water to replace the electron it loses, and the resulting electron flow pumps protons into the thylakoid lumen, whose return through ATP synthase makes ATP while NADP+ is reduced to NADPH.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Linkage and Recombination Frequency
concepts.summary: Genes on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together, and the farther apart they sit the more often crossing over separates them, so recombination frequency serves as a rough measure of map distance.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Logistic Growth and Carrying Capacity
concepts.summary: Logistic growth slows as population size approaches the carrying capacity K, because per-capita growth falls as competition for limited resources intensifies.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Loss of Control and Cancer
concepts.summary: Cancer begins when mutations disable checkpoint or repair genes so that cells divide without the usual signals, and a proto-oncogene becomes an oncogene when overactive while a tumour-suppressor gene must lose both copies.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Lowering Activation Energy
concepts.summary: An enzyme accelerates a reaction by stabilising the transition state and so lowering the activation energy, which raises the fraction of collisions that succeed without changing the equilibrium position.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Magnification, Resolution and Scale Bars
concepts.summary: Magnification is image size divided by actual size, but resolution sets the finest detail visible, so a scale bar converts a measured image length back into a real length.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Measuring Biodiversity at Three Levels
concepts.summary: Biodiversity is measured as genetic variation within a species, species richness within a community and the variety of ecosystems in a region, and each level can decline independently of the others.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Meiosis Halves the Chromosome Number
concepts.summary: One replication followed by two divisions produces four haploid cells, so each gamete carries one chromosome of every homologous pair instead of two.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Mendel's Law of Segregation
concepts.summary: A diploid organism carries two alleles per gene and they separate during meiosis so each gamete receives one, which is why a monohybrid cross between heterozygotes gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Mitochondria and Chloroplasts as Converters
concepts.summary: Mitochondria oxidise pyruvate in their matrix and use the extracted electrons to pump protons across the inner membrane, chloroplasts trap light in thylakoids, and both organelles carry their own DNA as the endosymbiotic theory predicts.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Molecular and Biogeographic Evidence
concepts.summary: Neutral gene sequences accumulate differences roughly in proportion to the time since two lineages diverged, and island species resemble the nearest mainland forms rather than distant species in a similar climate.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Multiple Alleles and Polygenic Traits
concepts.summary: A gene with more than two alleles in the population, such as ABO with three, still gives each diploid person only two, and a polygenic trait such as height varies continuously because many genes add small effects.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Natural Selection Requires Heritable Variation
concepts.summary: Natural selection changes allele frequencies only when individuals differ in heritable traits that affect survival or reproduction, so a population with no such variation cannot evolve by selection.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Neurons Signal by Electrical Gradients
concepts.summary: A neuron holds a resting potential near minus 70 millivolts by pumping sodium out and potassium in, and it fires an action potential once depolarisation reaches threshold.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Overexploitation and Invasive Species
concepts.summary: Harvesting a population faster than it reproduces drives it down, and an introduced species released from its natural predators can outcompete natives because nothing in the new community limits it.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Pathogens, Transmission and Antibiotic Resistance
concepts.summary: A pathogen causes disease by damaging tissue or releasing toxins, and bacteria survive an antibiotic only if they already carry resistance, so incomplete courses of treatment select for resistant strains.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: PCR Amplifies DNA In Vitro
concepts.summary: PCR cycles denaturation, primer annealing and extension so that each round doubles the target, which is why thirty cycles turn one molecule into about a billion copies.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Phases of the Cell Cycle
concepts.summary: Interphase occupies most of the cycle as G1, S and G2 with DNA replicated during S, and the mitotic phase then divides the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Phosphorus and Water as Material Cycles
concepts.summary: Phosphorus has no gaseous phase and moves from rock through soil and organisms by weathering and decomposition, while water cycles by evaporation, condensation and precipitation, so neither behaves like the carbon cycle.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Photorespiration and C4 or CAM Adaptations
concepts.summary: RuBisCO also binds oxygen, so the hot dry conditions that close stomata drive photorespiration, and C4 plants separate initial fixation from the Calvin cycle in space while CAM plants separate it in time.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Pleiotropy, Epistasis and Environment
concepts.summary: One gene can affect several traits, one gene can mask another, and the same genotype can yield different phenotypes in different environments, as hydrangea flower colour shifts with soil pH.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Point Mutations and Their Effects
concepts.summary: A substitution changes one base and may be silent, missense or nonsense, while an insertion or deletion that is not a multiple of three shifts the reading frame and usually destroys the protein.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Polar Covalent Bonds in Water
concepts.summary: Oxygen pulls the shared electrons of a water molecule toward itself, so the molecule carries partial charges and each molecule can hydrogen-bond with up to four neighbours.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Pollution and Eutrophication
concepts.summary: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus run off farmland into water, where the algal growth they fuel is decomposed by bacteria that consume the dissolved oxygen and create a hypoxic dead zone.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Positive Feedback Amplifies Change
concepts.summary: Positive feedback reinforces a deviation instead of reversing it, so it drives a process to completion, as oxytocin release does during labour, and cannot hold a steady state on its own.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Primary and Secondary Succession
concepts.summary: Primary succession starts on bare substrate with no soil and begins with pioneer species, while secondary succession follows a disturbance that leaves soil and seeds and therefore proceeds faster.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Probability Rules for Inheritance
concepts.summary: The probability that two independent events both occur is the product of their probabilities, so a cross between two heterozygotes gives one quarter homozygous recessive offspring rather than one half.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Productivity and Why It Limits Ecosystems
concepts.summary: Gross primary productivity is the total carbon fixed by producers and net primary productivity is what remains after their respiration, which is the energy budget available to every consumer.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Prokaryotes and Their Metabolic Range
concepts.summary: Bacteria and archaea lack a nucleus but cover almost every metabolic strategy, including nitrogen fixation and methanogenesis, which is why they drive the biogeochemical cycles.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Prokaryotic and Eukaryotic Cells
concepts.summary: A prokaryotic cell has no membrane-bound nucleus and keeps its DNA in a nucleoid, while a eukaryotic cell encloses its DNA in a nucleus and divides its labour among organelles.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Proofreading and Repair
concepts.summary: DNA polymerase proofreads as it copies and mismatch, base-excision and nucleotide-excision repair remove damage afterwards, so a faulty repair gene such as BRCA1 leaves mutations uncorrected.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Proteins and Nucleic Acids as Machinery and Information
concepts.summary: A protein's function follows its folded shape, which is fixed by its amino-acid sequence, while a nucleic acid stores that sequence as bases read three at a time.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Protists, Fungi and Plants
concepts.summary: Protists are eukaryotes outside the fungi, plants and animals and form several independent lineages, fungi absorb nutrients through external hyphae, and plants are multicellular photosynthesizers with cellulose walls.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Reading a Pedigree
concepts.summary: A pedigree traces a trait through a family, and a trait present in every generation of both sexes suggests dominance while one that skips generations and affects mostly males suggests X-linked recessiveness.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Reading a Phylogenetic Tree
concepts.summary: A phylogenetic tree records branching order rather than a ladder of progress, so two tips joined by a recent node are more closely related to each other than either is to a tip that branches earlier.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Reading a Punnett Square
concepts.summary: A Punnett square lists each parent's possible gametes along one axis and fills the boxes with their combinations, so the box counts give an expected ratio that only holds over many offspring.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Redox Carriers NAD+ and FAD
concepts.summary: NAD+ and FAD accept electrons and hydrogen at oxidation steps and deliver them to the electron transport chain, so their reduced forms carry the energy that later pumps protons.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Resistance, Resilience and Trophic Cascades
concepts.summary: A stable ecosystem resists change and recovers after it, and a trophic cascade shows that removing a top predator can change the abundance of every level beneath it.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Restriction Enzymes and Plasmids
concepts.summary: A restriction enzyme cuts DNA at a specific recognition sequence, and a plasmid cut with the same enzyme can carry a foreign gene into a bacterium that then expresses it.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Semiconservative Replication
concepts.summary: Helicase unwinds the helix, DNA polymerase copies each strand only in the five-prime to three-prime direction, and the lagging strand is built as Okazaki fragments that ligase later joins.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Set Points and Negative Feedback
concepts.summary: A negative feedback loop compares a measured value with a set point and reverses any deviation, which is how core temperature is held near 37 degrees Celsius when the environment changes.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Sex Chromosomes and Sex-Linked Traits
concepts.summary: A human female is XX and a male XY, so a recessive allele on the X chromosome shows in a son who inherits that X, while a daughter must inherit two copies to be affected.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Shared Features of Living Systems
concepts.topic: Characteristics of Life & Levels of Organization
concepts.summary: Living systems are organised, metabolise, respond to stimuli, maintain homeostasis, grow, reproduce and evolve, and a virus meets none of the metabolic criteria on its own, which is why its status as alive is debated.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: SI Units and Biological Scale
concepts.summary: Biology measures length in metres, mass in kilograms and volume in litres, and a cell 10 micrometres across is 10 to the minus five metres, so unit conversion is the first step in comparing structures.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Slope and Rate from a Graph
concepts.summary: The slope of a line is the change in the y-variable per unit change in the x-variable, so a steeper line means the measured quantity changes faster, not that it reaches a larger value.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Sources of Mutation and Their Consequences
concepts.summary: Mutations arise from replication errors, radiation and chemical mutagens, and only a mutation in a germ-line cell is inherited, which is why a somatic mutation can cause cancer in one body without passing to offspring.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Species Concepts and Reproductive Isolation
concepts.summary: The biological species concept defines a species as a group that interbreeds and produces fertile offspring, so reproductive isolation rather than physical difference is what keeps two species apart.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Stomata, Guard Cells and Water Loss
concepts.summary: Guard cells open a stoma when they take up water and become turgid, which admits carbon dioxide for photosynthesis but also lets water vapour escape, so the plant trades carbon gain against water loss.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Structure Fits Function at Every Scale
concepts.topic: Characteristics of Life & Levels of Organization
concepts.summary: A structure's shape constrains what it can do, so the thin flattened wall of an alveolus and the branching of a root hair both increase the surface available for exchange.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Sustainability as Living Within Regeneration Rates
concepts.summary: A practice is sustainable only if it uses renewable resources no faster than they regenerate and releases wastes no faster than they are absorbed, so a fishery can be harvested indefinitely only up to its maximum sustainable yield.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Synapses and Neurotransmitters
concepts.summary: An action potential releases neurotransmitter across a synapse, and the signal crosses in one direction only because vesicles sit on the presynaptic side and receptors on the postsynaptic side.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Temperature, pH and Inhibition
concepts.summary: Each enzyme works fastest in a narrow temperature and pH range because beyond it the bonds holding its tertiary structure break, and a competitive inhibitor occupies the active site while a noncompetitive one binds elsewhere and distorts it.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Test Crosses and Predicting Offspring
concepts.summary: A test cross with a homozygous recessive partner reveals an unknown dominant genotype, because any recessive offspring prove the unknown parent carried a recessive allele.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Active Site and Enzyme Specificity
concepts.summary: An enzyme binds its substrate in a pocket whose shape and charge match it, so a single amino-acid substitution in that pocket can abolish catalysis.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Calvin Cycle Fixes Carbon
concepts.summary: RuBisCO attaches carbon dioxide to RuBP in the stroma, and ATP and NADPH from the light reactions reduce the product to G3P, of which five of every six molecules go to regenerate RuBP.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Citric Acid Cycle and Oxidative Phosphorylation
concepts.summary: The citric acid cycle completes the oxidation of acetyl groups and loads NADH and FADH2, whose electrons drive the proton pumps of the inner membrane so that ATP synthase makes most of the cell's ATP.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Double Helix and Base Pairing
concepts.summary: Two antiparallel strands pair adenine with thymine by two hydrogen bonds and guanine with cytosine by three, so the sequence of one strand specifies the sequence of the other.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Fluid Mosaic Model
concepts.summary: A membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward, and its proteins, cholesterol and glycolipids move laterally within the sheet, which is what makes it fluid and mosaic.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Genetic Code Is Redundant and Non-overlapping
concepts.summary: Codons are read three bases at a time from a fixed start, 61 specify amino acids and three stop translation, so several codons can name one amino acid but a frameshift alters every codon after it.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Greenhouse Effect and Its Intensification
concepts.summary: Greenhouse gases absorb outgoing infrared radiation and re-emit part of it downward, and burning fossil fuel adds carbon dioxide that strengthens this absorption and warms the planet's energy budget.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Law of Independent Assortment
concepts.summary: Genes on different chromosomes assort independently, so a dihybrid cross between heterozygotes gives the 9:3:3:1 ratio, but genes close together on one chromosome do not.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Nucleus and Ribosomes
concepts.summary: The nucleus stores chromatin and assembles ribosomal subunits in its nucleolus, and the ribosomes it exports translate mRNA in the cytoplasm or on the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Operon as a Prokaryotic Switch
concepts.summary: In the lac operon a repressor blocks transcription when lactose is absent, and the genes are switched on only when lactose is present and glucose is low, so the cell builds the enzyme only when it pays.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The pH Scale and Biological Buffers
concepts.summary: pH is the negative logarithm of hydrogen-ion concentration, so one unit lower means ten times more hydrogen ions, and a buffer pair such as carbonic acid and bicarbonate holds pH near its pKa.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Shared Architecture of Energy Pathways
concepts.summary: Photosynthesis and respiration both run electron transport chains that pump protons across a membrane and both use the resulting gradient to make ATP, but they run in opposite directions from opposite electron sources.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Spindle and Chromosome Segregation
concepts.summary: Kinetochore microtubules attach each sister chromatid to the opposite pole, and tension from both attachments is what satisfies the spindle checkpoint before anaphase begins.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Stages of Mitosis
concepts.summary: Prophase condenses the chromosomes and breaks down the nuclear envelope, metaphase aligns them on the spindle equator, anaphase separates sister chromatids, and telophase rebuilds two nuclei.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Three Domains and Binomial Naming
concepts.summary: Life divides into Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya, and each species carries a two-part Latin name of genus and specific epithet, so Homo sapiens names one species within the genus Homo.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: The Three Statements of Cell Theory
concepts.summary: Cell theory holds that every organism consists of one or more cells, that the cell is the basic unit of life, and that all cells come from pre-existing cells by division.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Tissues, Organs and Organ Systems
concepts.summary: Similar specialised cells group into a tissue, tissues into an organ and organs into a system, so a function such as absorption is carried by a coordinated structure rather than by one cell type.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Transcription Makes an RNA Copy
concepts.summary: RNA polymerase binds a promoter, reads the template strand and builds a complementary RNA, and a eukaryotic transcript is capped, polyadenylated and spliced before it leaves the nucleus.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Translation on the Ribosome
concepts.summary: The ribosome holds the mRNA and matches each codon with a tRNA at the A site, catalyses the peptide bond, then translocates so the growing chain leaves through the exit tunnel.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Trophic Levels and the Ten Percent Rule
concepts.summary: Energy passes from producers to consumers along a food chain, and only about ten percent of the energy at one level is stored as biomass at the next, so food chains rarely exceed four or five links.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Types of Data and Their Displays
concepts.summary: Counts and categories are discrete data drawn as a bar chart, whereas measurements on a continuous scale are plotted as a line or scatter graph so the shape of the relationship is visible.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Why Biodiversity Has Value
concepts.summary: Biodiversity supplies ecosystem services such as pollination, water filtration and medicines, so its loss carries an economic cost as well as an ecological one.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Why Regulation Matters
concepts.summary: Every cell of an organism carries the same genes, so regulating when and where a gene is transcribed is what makes a liver cell different from a neuron.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Why Sex Persists
concepts.summary: Sexual reproduction costs the search for a mate and halves each parent's genetic contribution, but recombination and independent assortment generate the variation that selection needs when conditions change.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Why Small Cells Dominate
concepts.summary: As a cell grows its volume rises with the cube of its length while its surface rises only with the square, so exchange across the membrane cannot keep pace and the cell must stay small or divide.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology

concepts.title: Xylem and Phloem as Two Transport Tissues
concepts.summary: Xylem carries water and minerals upward from the roots, pulled by transpiration from the leaves, while phloem carries sugars from sources to sinks under pressure flow.

provenance.source: Biology - Cells, Genetics, Evolution and Ecology
